check_bank_insured.description: A plain yes or no on whether deposits at a bank are covered by FDIC insurance, with the date the cover began and a sentence you can send straight on to someone. Use it to gate a workflow: onboarding a vendor, checking where a payment is going, or verifying a customer's bank. A handful of institutions appear in the FDIC's register without being insured by it, and this separates them out rather than reading the field that says yes for every record. A bank that has closed answers no, and says where its accounts went.
check_bank_insured.display_name: Check whether a bank is FDIC-insured

Each merger names the other bank in it, so reading one bank's record tells you which bank it absorbed rather than repeating its own name back. The default leaves branch openings and closings out, because a large bank has thousands of them and they bury the handful of things that happened to the bank itself.

description: Look up any US bank from a workflow, straight from the FDIC. Find a bank by name, state or city, get its full record, and check in one step whether its deposits are FDIC-insured. Map its branches with addresses and coordinates, read its quarterly financials in dollars, see how much is on deposit at each branch, and trace what happened to it: who it merged with, what it used to be called, and whether it failed. Every failure since 1934 is here, as are industry totals for the whole country or one state, year by year. Names are resolved to the right bank rather than the closest-spelled one, figures come back in dollars, and dates come back as dates. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
